# 2.1 The modeling table

Checkpoint 2 uses only the 4,000 intensive care unit (ICU) stays in Set A and
`data/Outcomes-a.txt`. The modeling table has one row per stay. Each row contains
admission descriptors and summaries of measurements collected from hour 0
through hour 48. `In-hospital_death`, joined by `RecordID`, is the binary
outcome. The data are from the [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2012](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2012/1.0.0/)
(Silva et al., 2012; citation at the end of this report).

```{python}
#| label: read-set-a-only
set_a_files = sorted((DATA_DIR / "set-a").glob("*.txt"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem))
outcome_path = DATA_DIR / "Outcomes-a.txt"
assert len(set_a_files) == EXPECTED_N, "Set A must contain 4,000 records."
assert outcome_path.exists(), "Outcomes-a.txt is missing."

def read_record(path):
    frame = pd.read_csv(path)
    assert list(frame.columns) == ["Time", "Parameter", "Value"]
    record_id = int(path.stem)
    embedded = frame.loc[frame["Parameter"].eq("RecordID"), "Value"]
    assert len(embedded) == 1 and int(embedded.iloc[0]) == record_id
    frame["RecordID"] = record_id
    return frame

long_raw = pd.concat([read_record(path) for path in set_a_files], ignore_index=True)
long_raw = long_raw.loc[~long_raw["Parameter"].eq("RecordID")].copy()
time_parts = long_raw["Time"].str.split(":", expand=True).astype(float)
long_raw["hour"] = time_parts[0] + time_parts[1] / 60
long_raw["Value_raw"] = pd.to_numeric(long_raw["Value"], errors="coerce")
long_raw = long_raw[["RecordID", "hour", "Parameter", "Value_raw"]]
outcomes = pd.read_csv(outcome_path)[
    ["RecordID", "SAPS-I", "SOFA", "In-hospital_death"]
].copy()
assert len(outcomes) == EXPECTED_N and outcomes["RecordID"].nunique() == EXPECTED_N
assert set(outcomes["In-hospital_death"].unique()).issubset({0, 1})
assert long_raw["hour"].between(0, 48).all()
```

The Checkpoint 1 rule that negative values are invalid is retained. For
modeling, I additionally recode values outside broad physiologic screening
ranges as missing. This revises Checkpoint 1, where nonnegative outliers were
flagged but retained. Zero height and zero weight are now missing. The original
values remain in `Value_raw`, which makes every change auditable.

```{python}
#| label: clean-set-a
bounds = pd.DataFrame([
    ("Age", 18, 120), ("Height", 100, 230), ("Weight", 20, 400),
    ("HR", 20, 250), ("RespRate", 4, 60), ("Temp", 30, 43),
    ("pH", 6.8, 7.8), ("GCS", 3, 15), ("FiO2", .20, 1),
    ("SaO2", 50, 100), ("Gender", 0, 1), ("ICUType", 1, 4),
], columns=["Parameter", "lower", "upper"])
long = long_raw.merge(bounds, on="Parameter", how="left")
long["negative_invalid"] = long["Value_raw"].lt(0)
long["outside_screen"] = (
    long["lower"].notna()
    & (long["Value_raw"].lt(long["lower"]) | long["Value_raw"].gt(long["upper"]))
    & ~long["negative_invalid"]
)
long["Value"] = long["Value_raw"].mask(
    long["negative_invalid"] | long["outside_screen"]
)
cleaning_summary = (
    long.loc[long["negative_invalid"] | long["outside_screen"]]
    .groupby("Parameter", as_index=False)
    .agg(negative_codes=("negative_invalid", "sum"),
         outside_screening_range=("outside_screen", "sum"),
         total_set_missing=("Value_raw", "size"))
    .sort_values("total_set_missing", ascending=False)
)
display(cleaning_summary.style.hide(axis="index").set_caption(
    "Table 1. Values recoded as missing before feature construction"
))
```

Table 1 documents every cleaning change. Negative codes account for most
changes, while `outside_screening_range` identifies the additional broad
screening decisions used for modeling.

```{python}
#| label: build-modeling-table
static_parameters = ["Age", "Gender", "Height", "ICUType", "Weight"]
series_parameters = sorted(
    set(long["Parameter"].unique()) - {"Age", "Gender", "Height", "ICUType"}
)
static = (
    long.loc[long["hour"].eq(0) & long["Parameter"].isin(static_parameters)]
    .sort_values(["RecordID", "Parameter", "hour"])
    .drop_duplicates(["RecordID", "Parameter"], keep="first")
    .pivot(index="RecordID", columns="Parameter", values="Value")
    .rename(columns={"Weight": "Weight_admission"})
)
series = long.loc[long["Parameter"].isin(series_parameters)].copy()
series = series.sort_values(["RecordID", "Parameter", "hour"])
valid = series.dropna(subset=["Value"]).copy()
valid["time_value"] = valid["hour"] * valid["Value"]
valid["time_squared"] = valid["hour"] ** 2
series_summary = valid.groupby(["RecordID", "Parameter"]).agg(
    count=("Value", "size"), last=("Value", "last"),
    minimum=("Value", "min"), maximum=("Value", "max"), mean=("Value", "mean"),
    sum_time=("hour", "sum"), sum_value=("Value", "sum"),
    sum_time_value=("time_value", "sum"), sum_time_squared=("time_squared", "sum"),
)
denominator = series_summary["count"] * series_summary["sum_time_squared"] - series_summary["sum_time"] ** 2
series_summary["slope"] = (
    series_summary["count"] * series_summary["sum_time_value"]
    - series_summary["sum_time"] * series_summary["sum_value"]
) / denominator.replace(0, np.nan)
series_summary = series_summary[["count", "last", "minimum", "maximum", "mean", "slope"]]
complete_index = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
    [outcomes["RecordID"], series_parameters], names=["RecordID", "Parameter"]
)
series_summary = series_summary.reindex(complete_index)
series_summary["count"] = series_summary["count"].fillna(0).astype(int)
series_summary["never"] = series_summary["count"].eq(0).astype(int)
series_wide = series_summary.unstack("Parameter")
series_wide.columns = [f"{parameter}_{stat}" for stat, parameter in series_wide.columns]
modeling = (
    outcomes[["RecordID"]].set_index("RecordID")
    .join(static, how="left").join(series_wide, how="left")
    .join(outcomes.set_index("RecordID")[["SAPS-I", "SOFA", "In-hospital_death"]])
    .reset_index()
)
modeling["SAPS-I"] = modeling["SAPS-I"].replace(-1, np.nan)
modeling["SOFA"] = modeling["SOFA"].replace(-1, np.nan)
modeling["outcome"] = modeling.pop("In-hospital_death").astype(int)
for name in ["Height", "Weight_admission", "Age"]:
    modeling[f"{name}_missing"] = modeling[name].isna().astype(int)
modeling["Gender"] = modeling["Gender"].map({0: "Female", 1: "Male"}).fillna("Unknown")
modeling["ICUType"] = modeling["ICUType"].map({
    1: "Coronary care", 2: "Cardiac surgery recovery",
    3: "Medical ICU", 4: "Surgical ICU",
}).fillna("Unknown")
assert len(modeling) == EXPECTED_N
assert modeling["RecordID"].nunique() == EXPECTED_N
assert modeling["outcome"].notna().all()
modeling.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "cp2_modeling_table.csv", index=False)
n_deaths = int(modeling["outcome"].sum())
death_rate = modeling["outcome"].mean()
display(Markdown(
    f"The modeling table contains **{len(modeling):,} stays**, **{n_deaths:,} deaths**, "
    f"and an in-hospital mortality rate of **{death_rate:.1%}**. Its one-row-per-stay "
    "layout is checked explicitly, so ordinary stratified folds are also folds by stay."
))
```

# 2.2 Predictors

Only data from hours 0 through 48 are predictors. `RecordID` is an identifier;
length of stay and survival are not read into the modeling table; and SAPS-I and
SOFA are reserved as benchmarks. ICU type is categorical. The time-series
features retain current level, range, average level, linear direction,
measurement intensity, and whether a variable was never measured.

```{python}
#| label: predictor-groups
predictor_groups = pd.DataFrame([
    ("Admission descriptors", 5, "Baseline age, sex, body size, and ICU context."),
    ("Last, minimum, maximum, and mean", 4 * len(series_parameters), "Level and extremes summarize severity over 48 hours."),
    ("Slope", len(series_parameters), "Direction may distinguish improvement from deterioration."),
    ("Measurement count", len(series_parameters), "Monitoring intensity can reflect clinical concern."),
    ("Never-measured indicators", len(series_parameters) + 3, "Missingness can be informative."),
], columns=["Group", "Count", "Clinical reason"])
excluded_columns = ["RecordID", "outcome", "SAPS-I", "SOFA"]
feature_columns = [name for name in modeling.columns if name not in excluded_columns]
categorical_features = ["Gender", "ICUType"]
numeric_features = [name for name in feature_columns if name not in categorical_features]
X, y = modeling[feature_columns].copy(), modeling["outcome"].to_numpy()
predictor_groups.loc[len(predictor_groups)] = [
    "Total before categorical expansion", len(feature_columns),
    "Full candidate set used by Models 1 and 3."
]
display(predictor_groups.style.hide(axis="index").set_caption(
    "Table 2. Predictor groups and clinical rationale"
))
```

The count and never-measured features retain missingness information before
median imputation. No observed time-series parameter was dropped for being
rarely measured; the exclusion threshold was zero valid stays. This avoids
outcome-informed screening before CV. Constant columns are removed using
training data only.

# 2.3 Cross-validation design

I use five-fold stratified cross-validation. Every model and both
benchmarks use the same outer folds. LASSO and random-forest tuning use
three-fold CV inside each outer training fold and minimize Brier score. Median
imputation, constant-column removal, scaling, one-hot encoding, and tuning are
fit within training data and then applied to validation or held-out data.

```{python}
#| label: cross-validation-design
outer_cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=OUTER_K, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
outer_splits = list(outer_cv.split(X, y))
outer_fold = np.empty(len(y), dtype=int)
for fold, (_, test_index) in enumerate(outer_splits, start=1):
    outer_fold[test_index] = fold
fold_balance = (
    pd.DataFrame({"fold": outer_fold, "outcome": y}).value_counts(["fold", "outcome"])
    .unstack(fill_value=0).rename(columns={0: "Survived", 1: "Died"}).reset_index()
)
fold_balance["Death rate"] = fold_balance["Died"] / (fold_balance["Survived"] + fold_balance["Died"])
display(fold_balance.style.hide(axis="index").format({"Death rate": "{:.1%}"}).set_caption(
    "Table 3. Fixed outer folds shared by every model and benchmark"
))
```

Table 3 confirms successful stratification. Because there is one row per stay,
no stay can occur in both training and held-out data.

```{python}
#| label: model-definitions
category_levels = [
    ["Female", "Male", "Unknown"],
    ["Coronary care", "Cardiac surgery recovery", "Medical ICU", "Surgical ICU", "Unknown"],
]
def make_preprocessor(scale_numeric):
    steps = [("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="median"))]
    if scale_numeric:
        steps.append(("scale", StandardScaler()))
    return ColumnTransformer([
        ("numeric", Pipeline(steps), numeric_features),
        ("categorical", OneHotEncoder(categories=category_levels, handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False), categorical_features),
    ], sparse_threshold=0, verbose_feature_names_out=False)

def make_lasso_pipeline():
    return Pipeline([
        ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(True)), ("remove_constant", VarianceThreshold()),
        ("model", LogisticRegression(l1_ratio=1, solver="saga", max_iter=3000, random_state=SEED)),
    ])

def make_forest_pipeline():
    return Pipeline([
        ("preprocess", make_preprocessor(False)), ("remove_constant", VarianceThreshold()),
        ("model", RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=250, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=-1, class_weight="balanced_subsample")),
    ])

gam_continuous = [
    "Age", "HR_mean", "Temp_mean", "RespRate_mean", "MAP_mean",
    "Creatinine_last", "Lactate_last", "GCS_last", "BUN_last", "pH_last",
    "Urine_mean", "WBC_last",
]
gam_linear, gam_categories = ["MechVent_maximum"], ["Gender", "ICUType"]

def fit_gam_preprocessor(frame):
    imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy="median")
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(imputer.fit_transform(frame[gam_continuous]))
    linear_imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit(frame[gam_linear])
    encoder = OneHotEncoder(categories=category_levels, handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False).fit(frame[gam_categories])
    return {"continuous_imputer": imputer, "continuous_scaler": scaler,
            "linear_imputer": linear_imputer, "category_encoder": encoder}

def apply_gam_preprocessor(frame, prep):
    continuous = prep["continuous_scaler"].transform(prep["continuous_imputer"].transform(frame[gam_continuous]))
    linear = prep["linear_imputer"].transform(frame[gam_linear])
    categories = prep["category_encoder"].transform(frame[gam_categories])
    return np.column_stack([continuous, linear, categories])

def gam_terms():
    term = s(0, n_splines=4)
    for index in range(1, len(gam_continuous)):
        term += s(index, n_splines=4)
    for index in range(len(gam_continuous), len(gam_continuous) + 9):
        term += l(index)
    return term
```

# 2.4 Model 1: regularized logistic regression

Model 1 is logistic regression with a least absolute shrinkage and selection
operator (LASSO) penalty. LASSO is appropriate because the engineered feature
set is large and correlated: it shrinks weak coefficients to zero and produces
a more compact model. Twelve inverse penalty strengths (`C`) from 0.0032 to
3.1623 are compared within each outer training set. Numeric predictors are
standardized; categorical levels are represented by binary indicators.

```{python}
#| label: nested-cross-validation
C_GRID = np.logspace(-2.5, 0.5, 12)
FOREST_GRID = {"model__max_features": ["sqrt", 0.5], "model__min_samples_leaf": [5, 20]}
model_names = ["LASSO", "GAM", "Random forest", "SAPS-I", "SOFA"]
oof = pd.DataFrame({
    "RecordID": modeling["RecordID"], "outcome": y, "fold": outer_fold,
    "LASSO": np.nan, "GAM": np.nan, "Random forest": np.nan,
    "SAPS-I": modeling["SAPS-I"], "SOFA": modeling["SOFA"],
})
lasso_outer, lasso_selected, forest_outer = [], [], []

for fold, (train_index, test_index) in enumerate(outer_splits, start=1):
    X_train, X_test, y_train = X.iloc[train_index], X.iloc[test_index], y[train_index]
    inner_cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=INNER_K, shuffle=True, random_state=8000 + fold)
    lasso_search = GridSearchCV(
        make_lasso_pipeline(), {"model__C": C_GRID}, scoring="neg_brier_score",
        cv=inner_cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True,
    ).fit(X_train, y_train)
    oof.loc[test_index, "LASSO"] = lasso_search.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
    lasso_fit = lasso_search.best_estimator_
    all_names = lasso_fit.named_steps["preprocess"].get_feature_names_out()
    kept_names = all_names[lasso_fit.named_steps["remove_constant"].get_support()]
    coefficients = lasso_fit.named_steps["model"].coef_.ravel()
    selected = set(kept_names[~np.isclose(coefficients, 0)])
    lasso_selected.append(selected)
    lasso_outer.append({"Fold": fold, "C": lasso_search.best_params_["model__C"],
                        "Selected predictors": len(selected)})

    gam_prep = fit_gam_preprocessor(modeling.iloc[train_index])
    gam_train = apply_gam_preprocessor(modeling.iloc[train_index], gam_prep)
    gam_test = apply_gam_preprocessor(modeling.iloc[test_index], gam_prep)
    gam_fit = LogisticGAM(gam_terms(), lam=0.6, max_iter=300).fit(gam_train, y_train)
    oof.loc[test_index, "GAM"] = gam_fit.predict_proba(gam_test)

    forest_search = GridSearchCV(
        make_forest_pipeline(), FOREST_GRID, scoring="neg_brier_score",
        cv=inner_cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True,
    ).fit(X_train, y_train)
    oof.loc[test_index, "Random forest"] = forest_search.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
    forest_outer.append({
        "Fold": fold, "max_features": forest_search.best_params_["model__max_features"],
        "min_samples_leaf": forest_search.best_params_["model__min_samples_leaf"],
        "Inner mean Brier score": -forest_search.best_score_,
    })
assert oof[["LASSO", "GAM", "Random forest"]].notna().all().all()
```

```{python}
#| label: fit-final-models
full_inner_cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=OUTER_K, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
final_lasso_search = GridSearchCV(
    make_lasso_pipeline(), {"model__C": C_GRID}, scoring="neg_brier_score",
    cv=full_inner_cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True,
).fit(X, y)
final_lasso = final_lasso_search.best_estimator_
final_gam_prep = fit_gam_preprocessor(modeling)
final_gam_X = apply_gam_preprocessor(modeling, final_gam_prep)
final_gam = LogisticGAM(gam_terms(), lam=0.6, max_iter=300).fit(final_gam_X, y)
final_forest_search = GridSearchCV(
    make_forest_pipeline(), FOREST_GRID, scoring="neg_brier_score",
    cv=full_inner_cv, n_jobs=-1, refit=True,
).fit(X, y)
final_forest = final_forest_search.best_estimator_

all_final_names = final_lasso.named_steps["preprocess"].get_feature_names_out()
final_names = all_final_names[final_lasso.named_steps["remove_constant"].get_support()]
final_values = final_lasso.named_steps["model"].coef_.ravel()
final_coefficients = pd.DataFrame({"Predictor": final_names, "Coefficient": final_values})
final_coefficients = final_coefficients.loc[~np.isclose(final_coefficients["Coefficient"], 0)].copy()
final_coefficients["Folds selected"] = final_coefficients["Predictor"].map(
    lambda name: sum(name in selected for selected in lasso_selected)
)
final_coefficients["Absolute coefficient"] = final_coefficients["Coefficient"].abs()
final_coefficients = final_coefficients.sort_values("Absolute coefficient", ascending=False)
```

```{python}
#| label: lasso-selection-summary
lasso_outer_table = pd.DataFrame(lasso_outer)
display(lasso_outer_table.style.hide(axis="index").format({"C": "{:.4f}"}).set_caption(
    "Table 4. LASSO tuning and retained predictor count by outer fold"
))
```

Table 4 shows how the selected penalty and model size vary across folds.
Variation is expected with correlated summaries because LASSO can substitute
one related feature for another. Selection frequency describes stability and
should not be interpreted as causal importance.

```{python}
#| label: lasso-coefficients
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
coefficient_plot = final_coefficients.head(30).sort_values("Coefficient")
colors = np.where(coefficient_plot["Coefficient"].gt(0), "#b33b2e", "#2b6f9e")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
ax.barh(coefficient_plot["Predictor"], coefficient_plot["Coefficient"], color=colors)
ax.axvline(0, color="grey", linewidth=.8)
ax.set(title="Largest standardized coefficients in the final LASSO model",
       xlabel="Log-odds coefficient", ylabel="")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Figure 1 compares numeric predictors after standardization and categorical
indicator changes on their encoded scale. Positive coefficients correspond to
higher modeled mortality risk and negative coefficients to lower risk,
conditional on other retained predictors; the associations are not causal.

```{python}
#| label: lasso-kept-table
display(final_coefficients[["Predictor", "Coefficient", "Folds selected"]]
        .style.hide(axis="index").format({"Coefficient": "{:.4f}"})
        .set_caption("Table 5. Predictors retained by the final LASSO and outer-fold stability"))
```

Table 5 lists every predictor retained after refitting on all Set A. Features
selected in all five outer fits are more stable than those selected in only
one, although correlated features can lower apparent stability.

# 2.5 Model 2: non-linear effects with a GAM

Model 2 is a logistic generalized additive model (GAM). Twelve continuous
predictors were selected before fitting on clinical grounds to represent age,
vital signs, neurologic status, renal function, acid-base status, urine output,
and inflammation. Mechanical ventilation, sex, and ICU type enter as linear or
categorical indicator terms. Four basis functions per smooth and a fixed
smoothing penalty of 0.6 limit flexibility without using held-out outcomes.

```{python}
#| label: gam-predictor-table
gam_predictor_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Predictor": gam_continuous + gam_linear + gam_categories,
    "Role": ["Smooth continuous effect"] * len(gam_continuous)
            + ["Linear binary effect"] + ["Categorical effect"] * 2,
})
display(gam_predictor_table.style.hide(axis="index").set_caption(
    "Table 6. Fifteen clinically selected GAM predictors"
))
```

The restricted set makes the GAM interpretable and reduces unstable smooths.
The choices were fixed before examining outer-fold performance.

```{python}
#| label: gam-partial-effects
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.2
partial_variables = [
    ("HR_mean", "Mean heart rate (beats/min)"),
    ("Temp_mean", "Mean temperature (degrees C)"),
    ("Creatinine_last", "Last creatinine (mg/dL)"),
]
partial_rows, shape_rows = [], []
for variable, label in partial_variables:
    term_index = gam_continuous.index(variable)
    observed = modeling[variable].dropna()
    raw_grid = np.linspace(observed.quantile(.05), observed.quantile(.95), 100)
    reference_raw = observed.median()
    mean = final_gam_prep["continuous_scaler"].mean_[term_index]
    scale = final_gam_prep["continuous_scaler"].scale_[term_index]
    reference = np.nanmedian(final_gam_X, axis=0)
    grid_matrix = np.tile(reference, (len(raw_grid), 1))
    grid_matrix[:, term_index] = (raw_grid - mean) / scale
    reference_matrix = reference.reshape(1, -1).copy()
    reference_matrix[0, term_index] = (reference_raw - mean) / scale
    effect, interval = final_gam.partial_dependence(term=term_index, X=grid_matrix, width=.95)
    reference_effect = float(final_gam.partial_dependence(term=term_index, X=reference_matrix)[0])
    odds_ratio = np.exp(effect - reference_effect)
    partial_rows.append(pd.DataFrame({
        "variable": variable, "label": label, "value": raw_grid,
        "odds_ratio": odds_ratio, "lower": np.exp(interval[:, 0] - reference_effect),
        "upper": np.exp(interval[:, 1] - reference_effect),
    }))
    coef_indices = final_gam.terms.get_coef_indices(term_index)
    edf = float(final_gam.statistics_["edof_per_coef"][coef_indices].sum())
    left, middle, right = odds_ratio[0], odds_ratio[len(odds_ratio)//2], odds_ratio[-1]
    if edf < 1.3:
        direction = "increasing" if right > left else "decreasing"
        shape = f"approximately linear and {direction}"
    elif left > middle and right > middle:
        shape = "curved, with higher estimated risk at both low and high values"
    elif right > left:
        shape = "curved, with estimated risk generally increasing across the range"
    else:
        shape = "curved, with estimated risk generally decreasing across the range"
    shape_rows.append({"Predictor": label, "EDF": edf, "Assessment": shape})

partial_effects = pd.concat(partial_rows, ignore_index=True)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(8, 3.2))
for ax, (variable, label) in zip(axes, partial_variables):
    values = partial_effects.loc[partial_effects["variable"].eq(variable)]
    ax.fill_between(values["value"], values["lower"], values["upper"], color="#8ab6d6", alpha=.35)
    ax.plot(values["value"], values["odds_ratio"], color="#235f87")
    ax.axhline(1, linestyle="--", color="grey", linewidth=.8)
    ax.set_title(label); ax.set_xlabel("")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Odds ratio relative to median")
fig.suptitle("Adjusted GAM partial effects with pointwise 95% confidence bands", y=1.03)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: gam-shape-summary
shape_table = pd.DataFrame(shape_rows)
display(shape_table.style.hide(axis="index").format({"EDF": "{:.2f}"}).set_caption(
    "Table 7. Shape assessment for the plotted GAM effects"
))
clinical_text = {
    "Mean heart rate (beats/min)": "The increasing pattern is clinically plausible because tachycardia can reflect physiologic stress.",
    "Mean temperature (degrees C)": "The decreasing pattern suggests higher risk at lower temperatures, which is plausible for severe hypothermia; it does not show a U-shape over the central observed range.",
    "Last creatinine (mg/dL)": "The nearly flat, slightly decreasing pattern does not match the usual expectation that renal dysfunction raises risk, so it should not receive a strong clinical interpretation after multivariable adjustment.",
}
sentences = [f"- **{row['Predictor']}** is {row['Assessment']} (EDF {row['EDF']:.2f}). {clinical_text[row['Predictor']]}" for row in shape_rows]
display(Markdown("\n".join(sentences)))
```

Figure 2 and Table 7 describe the adjusted shape of each selected predictor.
Confidence bands widen where observations are sparse, so curve ends should be
interpreted cautiously.

# 2.6 Model 3: tree ensemble

Model 3 is a probability random forest using all candidate predictors. The
nested search compares `sqrt(p)` with 50% of features at each split and minimum
leaf sizes of 5 and 20, using 250 trees per fit. Missing values are
median-imputed within each training split. No early stopping is used.

```{python}
#| label: forest-tuning-table
forest_choices = pd.DataFrame(forest_outer)
display(forest_choices.style.hide(axis="index").format({"Inner mean Brier score": "{:.4f}"})
        .set_caption("Table 8. Random-forest settings chosen by nested tuning"))
```

Table 8 shows whether tuning consistently favors the same feature sampling and
terminal-node regularization across outer folds.

# 2.7 Comparison and choice of final model

```{python}
#| label: comparison-table
fold_rows = []
for model_name in model_names:
    for fold in range(1, OUTER_K + 1):
        mask = oof["fold"].eq(fold) & oof[model_name].notna()
        fold_rows.append({"Model": model_name, "Fold": fold,
                          "AUROC": roc_auc_score(oof.loc[mask, "outcome"], oof.loc[mask, model_name])})
fold_auc = pd.DataFrame(fold_rows)
auc_summary = (fold_auc.groupby("Model")["AUROC"].agg(**{"Mean AUROC": "mean", "SD AUROC": "std"}).reset_index())
comparison_table = (
    fold_auc.pivot(index="Model", columns="Fold", values="AUROC")
    .rename(columns=lambda value: f"Fold {value}").reset_index()
    .merge(auc_summary, on="Model").sort_values("Mean AUROC", ascending=False)
)
display(comparison_table.style.hide(axis="index").format(
    {column: "{:.3f}" for column in comparison_table.columns if column != "Model"})
    .set_caption("Table 9. Outer-fold AUROC for three models and two benchmarks"))
```

Table 9 compares every approach on the same held-out stays. Fold-to-fold
variation provides context for whether a small mean AUROC difference is
meaningful.

```{python}
#| label: roc-curves
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
for model_name in model_names:
    mask = oof[model_name].notna()
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(oof.loc[mask, "outcome"], oof.loc[mask, model_name])
    pooled_auc = roc_auc_score(oof.loc[mask, "outcome"], oof.loc[mask, model_name])
    ax.plot(fpr, tpr, label=f"{model_name} ({pooled_auc:.3f})")
ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--", color="grey")
ax.set(xlabel="False-positive rate", ylabel="True-positive rate",
       title="Out-of-fold receiver operating characteristic curves")
ax.legend(title="Pooled AUROC", loc="lower right")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Figure 3 shows discrimination over all thresholds. Curves closer to the upper
left rank deaths above survivors more consistently; overlap indicates similar
discrimination.

```{python}
#| label: choose-and-save-final-model
candidate_summary = auc_summary.loc[auc_summary["Model"].isin(["LASSO", "GAM", "Random forest"])].sort_values("Mean AUROC", ascending=False)
benchmark_summary = auc_summary.loc[auc_summary["Model"].isin(["SAPS-I", "SOFA"])].sort_values("Mean AUROC", ascending=False)
best_model, best_benchmark = candidate_summary.iloc[0], benchmark_summary.iloc[0]
difference = best_model["Mean AUROC"] - best_benchmark["Mean AUROC"]
benchmark_sd = best_benchmark["SD AUROC"]
if best_model["Model"] == "LASSO":
    final_bundle = {"model_name": "LASSO", "model": final_lasso,
                    "feature_columns": feature_columns, "feature_window_hours": (0, 48)}
elif best_model["Model"] == "GAM":
    final_bundle = {"model_name": "GAM", "model": final_gam,
                    "preprocessor": final_gam_prep, "continuous_features": gam_continuous,
                    "linear_features": gam_linear, "categorical_features": gam_categories,
                    "feature_window_hours": (0, 48)}
else:
    final_bundle = {"model_name": "Random forest", "model": final_forest,
                    "feature_columns": feature_columns, "feature_window_hours": (0, 48)}
joblib.dump(final_bundle, OUTPUT_DIR / "cp2_final_model.joblib")
oof.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "cp2_oof_predictions.csv", index=False)
fold_auc.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "cp2_cv_results.csv", index=False)
variation_statement = "larger than" if difference > benchmark_sd else "not larger than"
display(Markdown(
    f"The best fitted model was **{best_model['Model']}** with mean AUROC **{best_model['Mean AUROC']:.3f}** "
    f"(fold SD **{best_model['SD AUROC']:.3f}**). The stronger benchmark was **{best_benchmark['Model']}** "
    f"with mean AUROC **{best_benchmark['Mean AUROC']:.3f}** (fold SD **{benchmark_sd:.3f}**). "
    f"The difference of **{difference:.3f}** was **{variation_statement}** the benchmark's fold-to-fold SD. "
    "I selected the highest mean-AUROC model and refit it on all Set A because it offered the strongest "
    "observed discrimination; simplicity and interpretability remain relevant when differences are small."
))
```

The saved bundle contains the fitted preprocessing required by the selected
model. Calibration, decision curves, subgroup analyses, and SHAP-style
explanations are deferred to Checkpoint 3 as required.

```{python}
                    "cp2_cv_results.csv", "cp2_final_model.joblib"]

display(Markdown(
    f"The complete analysis took **{elapsed_minutes:.1f} minutes** in this run. "
    "All random splits and stochastic models use fixed seeds. The analysis reads only from `data/`, "
    "writes only under `output/`, and uses repository-relative paths."
))
```

From the repository root, reproduce the report with:

```text
pixi run --locked checkpoint2
```

The rendered report is `output/checkpoint2.html`. The modeling table, final
fitted model bundle, out-of-fold predictions, and per-fold results are saved
under `output/` for Checkpoint 3.
